standard.title: Listen and use voice features
standard.description: interact in informal and structured situations by listening while others speak and using features of voice including volume levels
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have developed oral interaction skills through home and play contexts. They have not yet been explicitly required to practise structured listening behaviours or to consciously vary and control voice features such as volume across different interaction contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can interact in both informal and structured situations — listening appropriately while others speak and controlling voice features including volume — across a range of classroom and social contexts.

nodes.label: Listening is active
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate active listening behaviours when others are speaking — attending without interrupting and showing they understand.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate listening without interrupting in one structured interaction (e.g. group discussion).
nodes.typical_width: Use active listening behaviours — listening without interrupting, looking at the speaker (where culturally appropriate), showing understanding; apply in pairs, small groups and whole-class contexts.
wider: Practise listening for a specific purpose — to answer a question, to find a detail — and report back what was heard
Explore how listening conventions differ across cultural contexts — including First Nations Australian conversational protocols where relevant to the class community
Apply active listening skills in play-based interaction and compare to structured discussion — noting similarities and differences
nodes.hinge_reason: Active listening is a prerequisite for the structured interaction in Node 3 — students who have not established listening behaviours cannot meaningfully participate in exchanges where they must listen, contribute and respond, since the listening component collapses.

response_modes.reason: Active listening is a behavioural habit requiring practice to become reliable. Students need repeated structured opportunities rather than broader contexts. Precision and consistency are what matter here.

success_criteria: Student listens without interrupting while another student or the teacher speaks.
Student can retell or respond to what was said, showing they were listening.

nodes.label: Volume varies by context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adjust their speaking volume appropriately for different contexts — indoor/outdoor, one-to-one, speaking to an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Use an appropriate volume level in one specified context (e.g. group discussion volume vs playground volume).
nodes.typical_width: Alter volume for different contexts — inside vs outside, informal interaction vs speaking to an audience; recognise that different contexts require different volume levels.
wider: Practise the same message at different volume levels across different contexts — comparing what feels appropriate in each
Explore other voice features — pacing, tone — and how they work alongside volume in different interaction contexts
Investigate how volume and voice norms differ across community and cultural contexts

response_modes.reason: Volume adjustment requires context-reading — students need exposure to multiple situations (inside, outside, audience) to generalise the principle rather than memorising a rule for one specific situation.

success_criteria: Student uses an appropriate volume level for the context without prompting.
Student can identify when their volume is too loud or too quiet and adjust.

nodes.label: Interact in structured and informal situations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in both informal and structured interaction situations — contributing ideas, exchanging with peers and following instructions — using appropriate listening and voice behaviours.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute at least one idea in a structured group discussion and listen to at least one other contribution.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in informal and structured situations — pair work, small groups, class discussions, play-based experiences; contribute ideas and questions; listen to others and respond; follow spoken instructions.
wider: Participate in a range of structured interaction formats — paired discussion, small group, whole class, and performance audience — applying appropriate behaviours in each
Engage in play-based interaction requiring imaginative use of spoken language across different roles
Lead a short interaction (e.g. ask a question to the group) and manage the response

response_modes.reason: Structured interaction requires simultaneously managing listening behaviours, voice features, and contribution — these previously practised skills must now work together in real interaction contexts.

success_criteria: Student can contribute an idea in a structured interaction without prompting.
Student demonstrates active listening while others speak.
Student uses an appropriate voice volume for the interaction context.
